meta.question: maximum along-track noise correlation length at which isolated drive-around direction error stays under 5 deg and under 10 deg, expressed in cm and in seconds at 1 cm/s

noise_model.source: imported from correlated_noise_sensitivity.py (make_noise, effective_sample_count, along_track_ds, SIGMA_TOT/W/C); that file was read and imported, never modified
noise_model.description: n = white(sigma_w) + stationary OU/AR(1) along-track drift (sigma_c, rho(ds) = exp(-ds/L)); total per-axis variance fixed at (0.50 nT)^2 for every L
noise_model.drift_axes: per-axis OU (each field component drifts coherently)
noise_model.iid_ref: pure white 0.50 nT, no correlated component (anchor)
noise_model.whole: L -> inf: per-survey per-axis static offset

inversion.part_1_naive: cold-start zero-reference weighted least squares, K = ls_operator(G); assumes i.i.d. noise internally even though the data are correlated. Magnetization components only, geometry fixed and exactly known. K=1 (3 free params) for the isolated outcrop, K=3 (9 free params) for the wall.
inversion.part_2_noise_aware: exact generalized least squares via a whitening transform applied to BOTH data and forward operator: C = sigma_w^2 I + sigma_c^2 exp(-|s_i-s_j|/L) per axis, C = Lc Lc^T, solve the Lc^-1-whitened system, giving (G^T C^-1 G)^-1 G^T C^-1 d. Matched noise draws against the naive arm.
inversion.beta_selection: none (closed-form least squares; no regularization, no beta)
inversion.stopping_criterion: none (direct linear solve); the normalized residual rms is reported instead

residual_rms_conventions.gls_whitened: sqrt(mean(r_white^2)) = sqrt(chi^2/nD) under the TRUE covariance
residual_rms_conventions.gls_iid_weighted: the GLS solution's residual re-scored with the i.i.d. weighting, for comparability with the naive column

inversion.part_2_exact_check: both estimators are unbiased, so the accuracy gap is entirely Cov_OLS = (G'G)^-1 G' C G (G'G)^-1 versus Cov_GLS = (G' C^-1 G)^-1. These are computed exactly (no Monte Carlo) alongside the relative Frobenius difference of the two estimator operators, so a null result cannot be confused with the whitening not having been applied

meta.threshold_definition: requirement is the largest L at which the ENSEMBLE-MEAN direction error is still at or below the threshold (median also reported for the isolated surveys)
meta.geometry_note: paper geometry: sensor at z = 0 in the body frame of the prism centred on the origin, i.e. mid-height of a 4x4x1 m prism standing on the ground (sensor 0.5 m above ground); drive-by x = -8..+8 m. 'sensor_height_m' in meta is the body-frame value. Run by analysis/a05_background_and_correlated_noise.py
